metadata.title: PCR-001: Standard PCR
metadata.purpose: Amplify a defined DNA segment from plasmid DNA, genomic DNA, cDNA, or purified PCR product using endpoint PCR. Written for a 50 uL Taq-style reaction; adaptable to high-fidelity polymerases by following enzyme-specific instructions.
metadata.scope: Standalone SOP for endpoint PCR. Not validated for qPCR quantitation, RT-PCR, or high-fidelity cloning workflows — see PCR-002 and PCR-003 for those.
beforeYouBegin: Use a clean pre-PCR workspace, fresh gloves, aerosol-resistant tips, and dedicated pre-PCR pipettes where possible.
Keep enzymes, master mixes, primers, dNTPs, and template on ice unless the manufacturer explicitly permits room-temperature setup.
Prepare a master mix for all shared components and add 5-10% excess volume for pipetting loss.
Add template last. For contamination-sensitive assays, load no-template controls last and keep amplified DNA away from setup areas.
Briefly centrifuge tubes or plates before cycling so liquid is collected at the bottom and bubbles are removed.

materials.name: Template DNA
materials.specification: Plasmid, genomic DNA, cDNA, purified amplicon, or validated control template

materials.name: Forward primer
materials.specification: 18-24 nt, 40-60% GC, Tm within 5°C of reverse primer
materials.storage: Store at -20°C; keep on ice during use

materials.name: Reverse primer
materials.specification: 18-24 nt, 40-60% GC, Tm within 5°C of forward primer
materials.storage: Store at -20°C; keep on ice during use

materials.name: 10X PCR buffer with MgCl2
materials.storage: Store at -20°C; keep on ice during use

materials.name: dNTP mix
materials.specification: Final concentration 200 uM each in reaction

materials.name: Taq DNA polymerase
materials.storage: Store at -20°C; keep on ice; do NOT vortex

tables.title: Cycling Program
rows: Optimize by gradient if weak or nonspecific

tables.title: Primer Design Checklist
rows: Longer primers may be required for cloning tails; calculate Tm from the annealing region
Avoid very low GC, long single-base runs, and strong hairpins
Use one consistent Tm calculator for both primers
Avoid 3′ complementarity between primers; a weak GC clamp can help
Routine endpoint PCR: 100 bp to several kb; long products need enzyme-specific optimization

steps.action: Thaw buffer, dNTPs, primers, water, and template on ice. Mix compatible reagents gently and briefly spin down.
steps.criticalNotes: Do NOT vortex enzyme. Mix by gentle flicking or pipetting.
steps.expectedResult: All reagents thawed and collected at tube bottom.

steps.action: Label tubes or plate wells. Include an NTC and a positive control before starting the run.
steps.expectedResult: Labeled reaction vessels with clear sample map.

steps.action: Calculate master mix volumes for all shared components except template. Add 5-10% overage.
steps.expectedResult: Master mix calculation complete for N + 1 reactions.

steps.action: Add water, buffer, dNTPs, primers, and polymerase to the master mix tube. Mix gently without foaming.
steps.criticalNotes: Add polymerase last to the master mix. Do NOT vortex — mix by gentle pipetting.
steps.expectedResult: Homogeneous master mix ready for aliquoting.

steps.action: Dispense master mix into tubes/wells. Add template DNA last. Add nuclease-free water instead of template to the NTC.
steps.criticalNotes: Add template last. Load NTC last to minimize contamination risk.

steps.action: Seal tubes/plate, briefly centrifuge, and place in the thermal cycler.
steps.expectedResult: Liquid collected at bottom, no bubbles, tubes seated in cycler block.

steps.action: Run the cycling program (or enzyme-specific program).

repeat.notes: 25-35 cycles typical; adjust by template abundance

steps.action: Analyze 2-5 uL product on agarose gel with a DNA ladder covering the expected product size.
steps.expectedResult: Single band at expected size in sample lanes.

steps.action: Accept a run when the expected sample band appears, the positive control works, and the NTC has no target-size band.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Single band at expected molecular weight

steps.expectedResult: Run accepted; proceed to downstream use.

steps.action: If the product will be cloned or sequenced, purify by PCR cleanup or gel extraction depending on specificity.
steps.expectedResult: Purified PCR product ready for downstream application.

controls.name: No-template control (NTC)
controls.description: Detect reagent, water, primer, or setup contamination. No target-size band expected.

controls.name: Positive control
controls.description: Verify that the assay, master mix, template handling, cycling program, and detection method work. Expected band should appear.

controls.name: Replicates
controls.description: Assess precision and pipetting consistency. Consistent band pattern expected across replicates.

expectedOutputs: Single band at the expected amplicon size on agarose gel.
Positive control band at expected size.
Complete run record with sample map, reagent lots, cycling program, and gel image.

troubleshooting.cause: Wrong annealing temperature, missing component, degraded template, inhibitors, insufficient extension
troubleshooting.solution: Verify setup map; lower annealing or run gradient; increase extension time; dilute template to reduce inhibitors; use fresh enzyme

troubleshooting.cause: Annealing too low, excess template/primer, nonspecific primer binding
troubleshooting.solution: Raise annealing temperature; reduce template or primer; use hot-start polymerase; redesign primers

troubleshooting.cause: Overcycling, degraded template, nonspecific amplification, overloaded gel
troubleshooting.solution: Reduce cycles; improve template quality; optimize annealing; load less product

troubleshooting.cause: Primer complementarity or high primer concentration
troubleshooting.solution: Reduce primer to 0.2-0.3 uM or redesign primers

safety: Ethidium bromide or alternative DNA stains may be mutagenic — wear gloves when handling gels and follow institutional disposal rules.
UV transilluminators emit UV radiation — use eye and skin protection.
